bib.title: The Impact of Positional Encoding on Length Generalization in Transformers
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2023 (37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; proofs in C.1/C.2 and Appendix B read in part (equations); perplexity tables 3/4 beyond the first buckets and figure-only plots (F.3-F.15) not read in detail.

question: How do different positional encodings (APE, T5 relative bias, ALiBi, Rotary, none) affect length generalization of decoder-only Transformers on downstream reasoning and mathematical tasks, with and without scratchpad?
hypothesis: Implied: explicit positional encodings may not be needed in decoder-only Transformers because causal masking lets them infer position, and may generalize to longer lengths at least as well as explicit PEs.
contributions: Systematic comparison of five PE schemes on length generalization over 10 tasks, 3 seeds each
NoPE outperforms explicit PEs; among explicit PEs T5's Relative PE is best, Rotary and APE worst
Theorems showing NoPE can represent absolute and relative PE; empirically it resembles T5's Relative PE attention
Scratchpad is task dependent and format sensitive; does not make the PE choice irrelevant

method.summary: Train a ~107M-parameter GPT-style decoder-only Transformer from scratch per task and per PE scheme on synthetic algorithmic tasks with training lengths up to L and test lengths up to 2L, scoring exact match. Also analyse attention-pattern distance between NoPE and other PEs, vary scratchpad formats, and (post-submission) pretrain 1.3B code LMs with ALiBi, Rotary and NoPE.
method.task: length generalization on synthetic sequence-to-sequence tasks (copy, reverse, addition, polynomial evaluation, sorting, summation, parity, LEGO, SCAN, PCFG)

datasets.name: Generated tasks (Copy, Reverse, Addition, Polynomial Eval., Sorting, Summation, Parity, LEGO)
datasets.size: 100K train examples and 10K test examples per task; 15% of train held out as validation
datasets.split: train lengths sampled from U(1, L), test lengths from U(1, 2L), L = 20 (L = 8 for scratchpad tasks)
datasets.source: generated by the authors following Nye et al. 2021, Saxton et al. 2019, Anil et al. 2022, Zhang et al. 2023
datasets.preprocessing: digits and symbols space-separated so the tokenizer does not merge them; modulo 10 for polynomial and summation

datasets.name: SCAN
datasets.split: length generalization split of the dataset

datasets.name: PCFG
datasets.split: length generalization split of the dataset

datasets.name: StarCoder subset (1.3B pretraining)
datasets.preprocessing: StarCoder tokenizer, vocab 49,152; mix 40% Python, 25% Java, 25% JavaScript, 5% GitHub issues, 5% GitHub commits

models.name: Decoder-only Transformer, HuggingFace 'base' config, with APE (sinusoidal) / T5 Relative Bias / ALiBi / Rotary / NoPE

training.objective: autoregressive language modeling log p(y|x) = sum_t log p(y_t | x, y_<t)
training.optimizer: AdamW (small models); AdamW beta1=0.9, beta2=0.95, eps=1e-8 (1.3B)
training.hardware: single-GPU runs on a mix of NVIDIA V100 32G, RTX8000 48G, A100 40G and A100 80G
training.wall_clock: 6 to 15 hours per run per seed on average

other.hparam_search: initial exploration lr in {1e-5, 3e-5, 5e-5} and weight decay in {0, 0.05, 0.1} showed no significant difference

inference.samples: 3 seeds per dataset-PE pair; one greedy output per item
inference.prompting: fixed text templates per task (Table 1), e.g. 'Compute: ... ?' -> 'The answer is ...'; scratchpad variants add <scratch> steps

parameters.scratchpad_components: Step Input, Step Computation, Step Output, Intermediate Variable Updates, Remaining Input; formats made by disabling components, plus Minimal (Compute+Output)

other.perplexity_eval_1.3B: 1500 validation documents, perplexity of last up to 200 tokens, context sizes 512 to 2560

metrics.name: Exact-match accuracy
metrics.definition: answer matches ground truth, reported per length bucket

metrics.name: Mean (reciprocal) rank across PEs
metrics.definition: mean ranking of each PE against the others over tasks and scenarios, following Liang et al. 2022 (HELM)

metrics.name: Attention head distance D(l)(A,B)
metrics.definition: minimum over head pairs at layer l of mean-over-positions Jensen-Shannon divergence between attention distributions

metrics.name: Perplexity vs context size (1.3B)
metrics.definition: perplexity of last tokens of code files at varying context sizes

eval.protocol: Train on lengths <= L, test on lengths up to 2L (I.I.D. and out-of-distribution buckets); 10 tasks, 3 seeds per dataset-PE pair; no significance test stated.

availability.data: generated by released code; SCAN and PCFG public

results.claim: NoPE has the best aggregate ranking across 10 length-generalization tasks.
results.setup: Decoder-only ~107M model trained from scratch per task, L=20, tested to 2L, exact match
results.quote: This figure shows aggregate ranking of positional encoding methods across 10 tasks.
results.table: Figure 1 bar labels: 0.22, 0.33, 0.50, 0.55, 0.69 (APE, Rotary, ALiBi, T5, NoPE)
results.note: Values read from figure labels in the text dump; the mapping to methods follows the bar order in the legend.

results.claim: Among explicit PEs, T5's Relative Bias generalizes best; ALiBi is mid-pack; APE and Rotary generalize poorly.
results.quote: ALiBi positions itself in the middle of the pack, while APE and Rotary show poor generalization performance.

results.claim: NoPE matches or beats the best explicit PE without additional attention computation.
results.quote: performs on par with or even better than the best-performing explicit PE, T5’s Relative Bias

results.claim: Rotary behaves more like APE than like other relative schemes in length generalization.
results.setup: Same as above; also attention distance distribution (Fig 7)
results.quote: our results show that it performs more similarly to APE than to other relative schemes

results.claim: All PEs fit the training lengths near-perfectly, so I.I.D. evaluation does not separate them.
results.quote: models achieve a perfect or near-perfect accuracy (Figure 3) on the I.I.D. lengths

results.claim: NoPE attention patterns are closest to T5's Relative PE and furthest from APE and Rotary.
results.setup: SCAN instances, per layer and per length bucket; NoPE with another seed is the baseline
results.quote: We find that NoPE’s attention patterns are most similar to that of T5’s Relative PE, and least similar to APE and Rotary.

results.claim: Theory: a NoPE first layer can recover absolute positions, and later layers can implement relative encoding.
results.setup: Constructive existence proofs (Theorems 1 and 2), Appendix C
results.quote: the first layer of fθ can recover absolute positions
results.note: Existence proofs only; they do not show SGD finds these weights.

results.claim: Scratchpad helps only the addition task, across PEs and formats.
results.setup: Six math/reasoning tasks, 8 scratchpad format variants, L=8
results.quote: scratchpad is beneficial solely for the addition task

results.claim: In scratchpad addition, NoPE and T5 RPE show bimodal short- and long-range attention, ALiBi favours short range, Rotary resembles APE (more uniform).
results.setup: Addition + full scratchpad, averaged over layers and heads
results.quote: NoPE and T5’s Relative PE resemble each other and exhibit a bimodal distribution

results.claim: At 1.3B code pretraining, Rotary perplexity explodes beyond training context while NoPE and ALiBi generalize to roughly 2x context.
results.setup: 1.3B models, context 1024, 30B StarCoder tokens, eval contexts 512-2560
results.quote: Rotary fails to generalize as its perplexity explodes.
results.note: Appendix F says NoPE and ALiBi generalize up to 1800 context; ALiBi more stable beyond.
results.where: Sec 7 'Scaling up to 1B models', App F.3

results.claim: Rotary perplexity at context 1400 in the [1500,1750] length bucket is 251.684 versus NoPE 2.121 and ALiBi 2.307.
results.table: Table 3, Length Bucket [1500, 1750], row Rotary, context 1400

results.claim: Fine-tuning the 1.3B models on the paper's task datasets gave identical performance across PE variants, because instance lengths are much shorter than the training context.
results.quote: yielded to identical performance among PE variants

results.claim: Reported cost of T5 relative bias: training and inference up to almost two times slower than APE.
results.setup: As reported by Press et al.
results.quote: can make the training and inference time of the model almost two times slower than the Transformer with APE

limits: No large-scale pretrained models with different PEs were available; main experiments use ~107M models trained from scratch on synthetic tasks (Limitations).
1.3B experiments are preliminary, language modelling perplexity only; a comprehensive downstream evaluation is left to future work.
Theory shows NoPE can represent absolute and relative PE (existence), not that training finds it; relative-PE claim rests on attention-distance similarity.
Only L=20 (L=8 for scratchpad); one hyperparameter set for all PEs; no significance tests stated.
Perplexity can mislead on length generalization (ALiBi recency bias; Chi et al. 2023 window-mask replication).

figures.caption: No positional encoding (NoPE) outperforms all other positional encodings at length generalization of decoder-only Transformers (GPT-style) trained from scratch and evaluated on a battery of reasoning-like downstream tasks.
figures.why: One bar chart ranks the five PEs: NoPE 0.69 > T5 0.55 > ALiBi 0.50 > Rotary 0.33 > APE 0.22.

figures.caption: Showcasing the generalization behavior of different positional encodings on 6 datasets.
figures.why: Accuracy vs problem length shows the drop beyond training lengths per PE.

figures.caption: Distribution of the normalized distance between the query and the key of the self-attention (addition task + full scratchpad).
figures.why: Shows bimodal attention for NoPE and T5 versus recency for ALiBi.
